page: Amazon Web Services r8i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including AVX-512, AMX-Tile, and AMX-INT8. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local instance storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance testing shows strong single-threaded CPU capabilities alongside balanced multi-core execution. In synthetic processor evaluations, the instance scored 2019.0 in Geekbench single-core and 12700.0 in Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Single-threaded data handling is particularly pronounced, with gzip compression achieving 34.05 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.07 GB/sec, placing both in the upper performance quartile. Geekbench text processing delivered 2904.0 points, scoring in the top ten percent. Small-model large language model inference demonstrates notable efficiency, clocking 337.11 tokens per second during text generation on a 135M parameter model, benefiting from built-in matrix extensions.

Memory throughput tests record 120.82 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 61.36 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing a PassMark memory score of 2362.89. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET operations registered 29.31 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 29.51 GB/sec. Because local disk storage is absent, instances must connect to remote block or object storage, shifting I/O dependence entirely to network performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density per core minimizes expenditure overhead for RAM-bound systems without paying for excessive unused CPU cores. The configuration is optimal for in-memory caching layers, Redis and Memcached deployments, relational and non-relational database engines, data mining, and analytics pipelines requiring large working memory sets.
